newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil roasted coffee sales reflect higher prices.
newsitem.headline: Brazil roasted coffee sales reflect higher prices.

text.p: A survey by Brazil's Sao Paulo State Coffee Industry Union of 12 companies showed roasted coffee sales in May grew at a slower rate than in recent months, limited by high prices, the union said in a statement.
Sales in May grew only 1.2 percent over April and slipped 0.04 percent compared with the same month last year.
April sales by contrast rose 21.4 percent over March and 5.8 percent over the same month in 1996.
"These figures show that the consumer is not accepting the high prices which have been caused by lack of supply to the market," said union president Nathan Herszkowicz.
During the first five months of this year, sales rose 5.4 over January to May 1996, again down from a seven percent increase the previous month.
On a twelve-month basis, the volume sold represented a 12.7 percent rise to end-May 1997, compared with a 15.6 percent increase in the twelve months to April 1997.
